name: Tonga
summary_text: Tonga demands real caution from trans visitors. The Criminal Offences Act criminalises sodomy (10 years, plus corporal punishment on paper — unenforced in recent years) and also criminalises males “impersonating a female” while soliciting — a direct trans-expression statute on the books. Against that: Tonga has a visible leiti (trans-feminine) community with the famous Miss Galaxy pageant (documented by the Washington Post in 2024), family and church networks that are devout but not systematically violent, and no documented recent prosecutions.

sources.title: Tonga | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): the Criminal Offences Act outlaws same-sex activity (max 10 years, no recent enforcement evidence) and criminalises male 'impersonation' of a female for an 'immoral purpose'; no gender recognition; intersex people unprotected; traditionally supportive culture of fakaleiti/fakafefine ('like a lady'), though rising conservatism threatens this.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (timeout); the underlying Washington Post piece (Aug 2024) covers Tonga's trans pageant and LGBT rights.

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Tonga: domestic violence, discrimination against women and corruption were the most prevalent problems; no reports of government abuses; the LGBT section notes the criminalisation of sodomy but rare enforcement.

sources.title: Cyclone seriously damages Tonga LGBTI center, shelter
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Feb 2018): Cyclone Gita seriously damaged Tonga's LGBTI centre and shelter - the community hub serving leiti and LGBTI Tongans.
